question: What colour is snow?

This happens because fresh snow consists of countless tiny ice crystals that reflect and scatter all wavelengths of visible light equally. When all colors of light mix together, our eyes perceive them as white. 

In very deep or pure ice (like glaciers), snow can appear blue because longer wavelengths (red) are absorbed more than shorter ones (blue), but fresh snow on the ground is almost always described as white.
